composition.serve_who: This sheet (108-01-515-001 "Raw Water System Schematic") is the Raw Water (seawater cooling) System diagram for the vessel's engine room and seachest, covering: port/stbd generator raw water cooling, main system heat exchangers (port/stbd), hydraulic pumps heat exchanger, pitch control (CPP) heat exchanger, aircon and watermaker seawater supply, seachest with strainers/valves feeding all these raw water consumers, and the boiler internal heat exchangers fed via fresh water loop off the FWD/AFT boilers. Evidence: titled "RAW WATER SYSTEM SCHEMATIC", drawing no. 108-01-515-001, seachest box labelled SEACHEST 001-01, dedicated pump data table "RAW WATER SYSTEM PUMP DATA", and BOM table listing seachest, strainers, valves, heat exchangers, pumps by item number matching the raw-water system class (515).

equipment_groups.placement_reasoning: No dedicated seachest node exists in the register; the seachest is the shared raw-water intake infrastructure feeding all raw water consumers (generators, main coolers, hydraulics cooler, CPP cooler, aircon, watermaker). It is titled 'SEACHEST 001-01' on sheet and carries the sea chest strainers, inlet/outlet valves, and the Cathelco galvanic protection control unit. Attached here provisionally to the raw-water sensors/monitoring node as the closest fit since no dedicated seachest/system node exists in the register; treat as infrastructure serving the whole raw water system.

functions.label: Seawater intake & distribution via seachest
functions.what_it_does: Draws raw seawater through hull seachest strainers (port & stbd) and distributes it via the main branch manifold and a flush connection point to all raw-water consumers (generators, main system heat exchangers, hydraulics pump HX, CPP HX, aircon, watermaker). Includes galvanic protection of the seachest via Cathelco unit and breather lines routed to the E-R vent box.
functions.sheet_region: Right-hand 'SEACHEST 001-01' dashed box, sheet top-right to mid-right

flow_scenarios.path: Seawater inlet (below DWL) → seawater strainer (port or stbd) → 3-way/2-way valves on main branch manifold → distribution via th25/th51 flex hose lines to main cooling seawater pumps, generator raw water pumps, hydraulics/CPP heat exchangers, aircon and watermaker strainers
Flush connection point on main branch manifold allows fresh water or external source to be introduced to flush the seawater circuit and remove fouling (per Note 3), bypassing normal seachest suction
Seachest air/vent lines run to E-R vent box (ref DWG 108-01-508-001) to prevent airlock

key_components: Cathelco Galvanic Protection Control Unit (galvanic protection of seachest)
functions.dry_data: Seachest class SWS-custom per BOM item 001; strainer ART 1166 1-1/2" (GDI112); ball valves ART 2070 1-1/2" (GDI312) and 1" chrome (BAL004D); cathodic protection: Cathelco Nano 3 system (CATH-NANOSYS).

facts: Main branch manifold within seachest distributes seawater to multiple consumers via 2-way/3-way valves — this is shared distribution infrastructure, not equipment.
Pipe legend defines flex/metallic pipe codes (th25, th40, th51, gy16, sea42, sea54, mw19/25/32/38/51) used throughout sheet with material/rating from Pipe Details table.

Breather/vent lines from multiple components (anti-siphon manifolds, seachest valves, boilers) all route to a common 'E-R Vent Box' referenced on DWG 108-01-508-001 — shared vent infrastructure, not itself equipment.
Priming lines from fresh water supply (ref DWG 108-01-510-01) assist priming of MCSWP-P and MCSWP-S — cross-reference to fresh water system, not detailed on this sheet.

uncertainties: The register's '511-water-heaters' node covers only 'FWD Water Heater (Owners Cab.)' and 'AFT Water Heater (Port Guest Cab.)' — unclear whether these correspond exactly to the 80L FWD/AFT boilers shown on this raw-water sheet (which are heated via engine coolant, not raw seawater); attached provisionally, but equipment identity match should be confirmed.

Seachest system has no dedicated system/tank node in the register; provisionally attached to '515-ifm-raw-water-sensors' as closest raw-water-system fit — a dedicated seachest node may be more appropriate if one exists elsewhere.

Valve tag numbers (e.g. 017-01/017-02/017-03/017-04 'SEE NOTE 3', 018-01/018-02, 019-01 to 019-03) are partially cross-referenced only by note 3 (quick-coupling flush); exact valve function per number not fully distinguishable from image resolution.

Item quantities/weights for BOM items 002 (seawater strainer bottom inlet 1.5") and some ball valve items (004,006,007) are listed but not clearly tied to specific tag numbers on the schematic — left as sheet-table facts only.
Text near 'th25' bottom sheet flow arrow direction and CPP seawater pump valve numbering (005-04, 005-05, 005-06) partly overlaps illegible small print; exact NC/NO states for each not fully certain.
